newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour majority hits record at City bookmakers.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour majority hits record at City bookmakers.

text.p: Traders in the traditionally Conservative-supporting City of London raced on Monday to bet on a drubbing for the ruling party in the May 1 British election.

London's financial bookmakers said the predicted parliamentary majority for the opposition Labour Party had jumped almost overnight to its highest level since the election campaign kicked off six weeks ago.

"It's higher than it's been at any point in this campaign -- it's leaped about 22 (seats) in the last day," said Paul Barnett, political market maker at financial bookie City Index, who attributed the move to weekend press comment. "It's been pretty darn busy today."
The financial bookmakers take so-called "spreads bets" from traders hungry for complex, high-risk gambling.
City Index quoted Labour's majority at a bid/offer spread of 102-112 on Monday -- up from 74-84 on Friday -- meaning a punter expecting the winning margin to top that could go 'long' at 112.
They quoted the number of seats Labour would win at 380-386, with the Conservatives on 222-228.
IG Index put the Conservatives on 225-231, with Labour on 377-383 for a majority of 96-106.
"Punters are beginning to wake up," said Patrick Jay, head of IG Index's sports desk, which covers political betting.
"People have been ignoring the facts that are staring them in the face. The opinion polls, which are the best indicator you have...are putting the lead at 17 to 20 percent."
The latest poll, published on Monday, projected a Labour majority of 197 seats, a 19 percentage-point lead over the Conservatives who have held power since 1979.
A party needs 330 seats for an overall majority in the 659-seat House of Commons.
